summary: Iter61 — Messagerie commande (order-scoped threads). Backend: 13/13 PASSED (test_order_messaging.py): GET /api/orders/{oid|code}/thread/{customer|rider} creates/returns shared thread with correct key order:{id}|party and kind commande_{cliente|livreur}; works for both order code and UUID. 400 when order has no rider (rider party) or customer has no account id (customer party). 400 on invalid party. Rider access: 403 when accessing customer party of own order, 403 when accessing rider party of someone else's order (own rider party OK). POST send: text validation (empty → 400), staff message has from_kind=store, rider has from_kind=rider; rider send creates db notification type=order_message with title/msg/link containing /console/commandes/{code}?focus=order-messages. Two different staff (admin + manager Fatou Konaté) see the SAME conversation history (same id, same messages) and can both append — shared thread confirmed. Customer flow: GET /api/public/account/threads returns the commande_cliente thread for the order; POST /api/public/account/messages/send with conversation_id creates order_message notification visible to staff with proper link. Frontend verified on /console/commandes/DN-261005-1044?focus=order-messages: order-messages card renders with od-msg-tab-customer / od-msg-tab-rider tabs, od-msg-list, 4 quick-reply-customer-{i} + 4 quick-reply-rider-{i}, od-msg-input, od-msg-send, WhatsApp badge od-msg-wa on customer tab only. Send works and new message appears instantly in list; rider tab loads (empty thread → 'Pas encore de message'). Notification bell: 3 notif-order_message items present; clicking one navigates to /console/commandes/{code}?focus=order-messages and the order-messages card is rendered (card has data-focus-id=order-messages; useFocusParam adds .focus-flash for 3s then removes — animation runs ~3s). focus-flash class not visible at the +4s assertion point because animation already ended; that is expected per implementation.

issues: Pre-existing hydration warning <span> inside <option> (dev-tool wrapper, carried over since iter56, non-blocking).

critical_code_review_comments: routers/messagerie.py _order_thread uses a hard-coded participant {kind:'store', id:'store'} — fine as a sentinel but means per-staff read receipts cannot be computed on this virtual participant; current get_order_thread does mark each staff user as reader on messages which is correct, but conv.participants.store is a shared facade.

_notify_reply inserts a notification on EVERY reply (customer or rider) but there is no de-dup / batching window — a chatty customer could spam the staff notification feed. Consider throttling (e.g. only one unread notification per thread until acknowledged).

customer_send only triggers _notify_reply if conv.get('order_code') exists — order-scoped threads created via _order_thread do set order_code, but legacy boutique_cliente conversations created via send_message_core do NOT set order_code, so customer replies on legacy threads bypass notifications silently (likely intentional, worth a comment).

OrderThread.jsx polls every 10s via setInterval — fine; however component resets conv to null on every orderId/party change which flashes 'Chargement…' briefly even when switching tabs on the same order (minor UX).
No cleanup endpoint for test messages — TEST_* messages accumulate in conversations and notifications collections. Consider adding an admin maintenance endpoint or a Mongo cleanup script.
